name: window.focus
description: Bring the given window to the foreground. Returns the previously-foreground window's handle (so the caller can restore it later if desired).

handle.description: Window handle, e.g. 'win:0x1A2B', sourced from window.list / window.find.

prior_handle.description: Handle of the window that was foreground before the focus change. Empty string if there was no foreground window (rare).

x-implementations.name: set_foreground_window
x-implementations.description: Win32 `GetForegroundWindow` (capture prior) + `SetForegroundWindow` (request focus). Subject to foreground-lock restrictions on NT 5+ (`SystemParametersInfo(SPI_GETFOREGROUNDLOCKTIMEOUT)`); denied requests surface as `ERR lock_held`.

windows-modern.description: SetForegroundWindow with GetForegroundWindow capture. Foreground-lock restrictions apply: a process that hasn't received recent input is blocked from stealing focus, returning `ERR lock_held`. The agent does NOT bypass the lock — callers can use `AllowSetForegroundWindow` from a privileged helper if needed.

windows-classic.description: SetForegroundWindow with GetForegroundWindow capture. NT 4 has no foreground-lock — the call always succeeds for the caller's permission level. NT 5 (Win 2000) onwards behaves like windows-modern.
